chapters.summary: Paul testifies to God's comfort and deliverance in the midst of affliction, encourages believers to depend on God in suffering, and explains the honest motives behind his change of travel plans.
keyPoints: Paul blesses God as the Father of mercies and the God of all comfort, who comforts us in all our tribulation.
Paul recounts his own affliction and deliverance, testifying to God's faithfulness and sharing the comfort and hope that suffering can bring.
Paul explains why he did not yet come to Corinth, showing that he conducts himself in sincerity and by the grace of God, not according to the flesh.
chapters.application: In hard times, remember that God is the source of all comfort - and having been comforted, we in turn can comfort others. Let us conduct ourselves with sincerity, depending on God in faith rather than on our own designs.

chapters.summary: Paul explains why he did not visit Corinth again, and urges believers to forgive the one who sinned, lest Satan should get the advantage over them.
keyPoints: Paul reveals his sorrow and tears, written to show the depth of his love for the Corinthians.
He urges the believers to forgive and comfort the one who sinned and has repented, lest he be swallowed up with excessive sorrow.
Though a door was opened for Paul to preach at Troas, he had no rest in his spirit because he could not find Titus, so he took his leave and went on to Macedonia.
chapters.application: Let us treat those who have done wrong with love, forgiving and receiving them once they repent, so that they are not overwhelmed, and so that we give no foothold to the enemy.

chapters.summary: This chapter stresses that believers are Christ's living epistle, that ministers of the new covenant serve by the Spirit rather than the letter, and that we are being gradually transformed into the likeness of the Lord.
keyPoints: Believers are Christ's letter of recommendation, written on the heart, known and read by everyone.
Ministers of the new covenant serve not by the letter but by the Spirit, for the letter kills, but the Spirit gives life.
The veil has been taken away, and with open face we behold the Lord's glory, being changed into his likeness.
chapters.application: As we read Scripture and pray each day, let us ask the Spirit to enlighten us and remove the veil from our hearts, so that Christ's glory may gradually change us, and our lives may display the likeness of the Lord.

chapters.summary: Paul speaks of the faithfulness and suffering of a minister of the gospel, stressing that what he preaches is Christ, not himself, and looking forward to eternal glory.
keyPoints: Though Paul is persecuted, he does not lose heart, for he has received this ministry by God's mercy.
Preaching is meant to make Christ known, not to promote oneself, so that people may see the true light.
Though the outward man perishes, the inward man is renewed day by day, and our momentary affliction is working for us a far more exceeding and eternal weight of glory.
chapters.application: Whatever hardship we face, let us remember that it is Christ we proclaim. As our inner being is renewed in the Lord and our eyes are fixed on eternal glory, we can overcome our present, momentary afflictions.

chapters.summary: Paul speaks of believers groaning in this earthly body, yet assured of an eternal dwelling to come, and urges everyone to walk by faith, to be moved by the love of Christ, and to become ambassadors of reconciliation with God.
keyPoints: If our earthly house, this tabernacle, is dissolved, we have a building of God, a house not made with hands, eternal in the heavens.
We are always confident, and would rather be absent from the body and present with the Lord, for we walk by faith, not by sight.
The love of Christ constrains us, so that we no longer live for ourselves, but for him who died for us and rose again.
chapters.application: Though we live in this world, we carry within us an eternal hope. Whatever our circumstances, let us walk by faith, let the love of Christ be our motive, and live out a life of reconciliation as ambassadors of peace.

chapters.summary: Paul urges the Corinthian believers not to receive the grace of God in vain, to show themselves to be servants of God, and calls them to work together with God and to be set apart to him.
keyPoints: He urges believers not to receive God's grace in vain, but to seize the day of salvation.
Paul lists the many forms of endurance by which he has proven himself a servant of God.
He calls believers not to be unequally yoked with unbelievers, but to cleanse themselves.
chapters.application: Today, let us treasure the grace God has given, bear witness to the Lord in word and deed, keep ourselves far from sin, and live holy lives, so that God's name may be glorified.

chapters.summary: Paul urges the Corinthian believers to cleanse themselves, and rejoices that their godly sorrow produced repentance, sorrow that leads to salvation.
keyPoints: Believers should cleanse themselves from every defilement of body and spirit, perfecting holiness in the fear of God.
Paul rejoices that the Corinthians' sorrow was a godly sorrow, producing repentance that leads to salvation and leaves no regret.
Titus brought news of the Corinthians' longing, mourning, and zeal, which filled Paul with even greater joy.
chapters.application: Let us grieve over sin, but not wallow in self-reproach - God's grace can turn our sorrow into joy, cleansing us so that we may live holy lives.

chapters.summary: Paul holds up the example of the Macedonian churches to urge the Corinthians toward generous giving for the saints at Jerusalem, stressing that giving offered willingly is what pleases God.
keyPoints: Though the Macedonian churches were in great trial of affliction, they gave willingly, showing the abundance of grace at work in them.
Christ's poverty has become our riches, moving us to follow his example of self-giving.
Paul sends Titus and others to ensure the collection is handled honestly, to the glory of the Lord's name.
chapters.application: Let us follow Christ's example, helping those in need willingly and gladly, without reluctance or grudging, for God loves a cheerful giver.

chapters.summary: Paul encourages believers to give generously and cheerfully, stressing that God loves a willing giver, and promises to bless those who give with a cheerful heart.
keyPoints: Paul commends the Corinthians' readiness of mind, and urges them to complete this good work of giving.
He who sows sparingly will reap sparingly, and he who sows bountifully will reap bountifully - giving that is willing and cheerful is what God accepts.
God blesses the cheerful giver, making him abound in every good work, so that thanksgiving is given to God.
chapters.application: Giving is not measured by the amount but by the willingness of the heart. May God give us a cheerful heart to give, that as we share we may experience his grace, and thanksgiving may rise to God.

chapters.summary: Paul defends his apostolic authority, stressing that spiritual warfare is fought by the power of God, not by the flesh, and warns that whoever boasts should boast in the Lord.
keyPoints: Paul is meek and gentle, yet bold to use the authority God has given him to deal with the disobedient.
The weapons of our warfare are spiritual, mighty to pull down strongholds and to bring every thought into obedience to Christ.
He will not boast beyond his measure, but only according to the limit God has assigned him, boasting only in the Lord.
chapters.application: When facing criticism or challenges, let us depend on the power of God, holding to the truth with gentleness and love, not striving in the flesh, but seeking only to please the Lord.

chapters.summary: Paul is anxious for the sincere devotion of the Corinthian believers, is forced into boasting to counter the false apostles, shows that he has willingly suffered and taken no advantage of the church, and exposes Satan's schemes.
keyPoints: Paul is jealous over the church with a godly jealousy, fearing that believers may be led astray from their sincere devotion to Christ.
False apostles disguise themselves as apostles of Christ, and Paul is forced to list his own background and the sufferings he has endured.
Paul boasts not for personal gain but out of love for the church, and exposes how Satan himself masquerades as an angel of light.
chapters.application: Today let us hold fast to a sincere and undivided faith, not deceived by clever words. Let us follow Paul's example of willing, self-giving love that seeks no reward, discern truth from falsehood with humility and wisdom, and find our strength in the Lord amid affliction.

chapters.summary: Paul shares his revelation of the third heaven, and boasts instead in his weaknesses, for God's power is made perfect in human weakness.
keyPoints: Paul recounts being caught up to the third heaven fourteen years before.
Because the revelations were so great, a thorn was given him in the flesh, to keep him from becoming too exalted.
Paul boasts instead in his weaknesses, for the power of Christ rests upon him.
chapters.application: When we feel weak, let us not be discouraged, for God's grace is sufficient. In our hardships, we can depend on the power of Christ, learning to experience his strength made perfect in our weakness.

chapters.summary: Paul warns the church to examine itself, urges them to pursue completeness, and blesses them to remain always in the love of God.
keyPoints: Paul announces his coming third visit, stressing that every matter is to be established by the mouth of two or three witnesses.
He urges believers to examine themselves, to see whether they are in the faith, and whether Christ is in them.

In his closing exhortation Paul calls the believers to rejoice, to be complete, to be of good comfort, and to live in peace with one another, and he closes the letter with the blessing of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit.
chapters.application: Let us continually examine our life of faith, asking whether we truly live in Christ, and pursue peace and holiness, letting the love of God fill us, so that we may encourage one another in grace and live out a faithful witness.
